the number of CD45(+)CD14(+) monocytes was increased in diabetic subjects with a long duration of diabetes, and that the number of these cells expressing CD16, a marker of monocyte activation, was significantly decreased in diabetic subjects with diabetic complications.
the number of circulating proinflammatory monocytes (CD16) is significantly reduced in diabetic patients with complications compared to diabetic patients without complications.
the circulating monocytes of diabetic subjects with clinically significant complications are phenotypically different from those of diabetic subjects without complications.
